title: JSON Schema for optional fields is incorrect.
issue_body: ### Initial Checks - [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2 ### Description JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 explains the way to display optional (nullable) values. https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core.html#section-7.6.1-3 Example: ``` { "type": ["string", "null"], "maxLength": 255 } ``` But pydantic v2 displays it like: ``` { "anyOf": [ { "type": "string" }, { "type": "null" } ], } ``` The variant with `anyOf` displays strange in ReDoc For example ![image](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/assets/18316828/5b5d301f-152a-4827-aaf4-ac29b7c5cb5f) The `toll_free_phone` has `"type": ["string", "null"]`, and `after_hours_phone` has a schema with `anyOf` Also I faced an issues with other libraries that uses this JSON Schema. ### Example Code ```Python import json from pydantic import BaseModel class Model(BaseModel): field: str | None = None schema = Model.model_json_schema() print(json.dumps(schema, indent=4)) ``` ``` ### Python, Pydantic & OS Version ```Text pydantic version: 2.1.1 pydantic-core version: 2.4.0 pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false mimalloc=true install path: /Users/viktor/.virtualenvs/gv2/lib/python3.11/site-packages/pydantic python version: 3.11.3 (main, Apr 25 2023, 00:40:12) [Clang 14.0.3 (clang-1403.0.22.14.1)] platform: macOS-13.4.1-arm64-arm-64bit optional deps. installed: ['email-validator', 'typing-extensions'] ``` Selected Assignee: @hramezani --- PR Context (#12147): ## Change Summary Fixes (partially) https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/7161. A new `union_format` parameter is added to the JSON Schema generation logic, defaulting `'any_of'` (the current behavior): ```python from typing import Annotated from pydantic import BaseModel, Field class Sub(BaseModel): ... class Model(BaseModel): a: int | None b: bool | str c: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=3)] | Annotated[str, Field(min_length=5)] d: list[int] | None e: Sub | None Model.model_json_schema(union_format='primitive_type_array') { │ '$defs': {'Sub': {'properties': {}, 'title': 'Sub', 'type': 'object'}}, │ 'properties': { │ │ 'a': {'title': 'A', 'type': ['integer', 'null']}, │ │ 'b': {'title': 'B', 'type': ['boolean', 'string']}, │ │ 'c': {'anyOf': [{'maxLength': 3, 'type': 'string'}, {'minLength': 5, 'type': 'string'}], 'title': 'C'}, │ │ 'd': {'anyOf': [{'items': {'type': 'integer'}, 'type': 'array'}, {'type': 'null'}], 'title': 'D'}, │ │ 'e': {'anyOf': [{'$ref': '#/$defs/Sub'}, {'type': 'null'}]} │ }, │ 'required': ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'], │ 'title': 'Model', │ 'type': 'object' } ``` It only combines unions into a `type` array when using primitives (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) _and_ when no metadata/constraints are used, otherwise fall backs to `anyOf`. We could also also apply this logic for non-primitives (e.g. arrays), but it can look a bit confusing depending on the tools consuming the JSON Schema. Taking [Swagger UI](https://swagger.io/tools/swagger-ui/) and [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc): | JSON Schema | Swagger UI | Redoc | |--------|--------|--------| |[^1] | | | | [^2] | | | |[^3] | | | | [^4]| | | For this reason, I went with this `'primitive_type_array'` option. If we want to extend this in the future, we could add a new `'type_array'` option that would also use the type array form if non-primitive types are being used (although apart from `"array"` types, I'm not sure this will be really useful as most `"object"` types come from model/dataclasses/typeddicts, which are referenced types and wouldn't be inlined anyway). In the issue thread, it was mentioned to use `oneOf` as well, but I don't think it makes sense to make use of it (even if we are guaranteed that the union members are exclusive, such as ` | None`). `oneOf` means that it successfully validates if _one and only one_ member of the union validates, but this is not how Pydantic performs validation of union types. Depending on the [union mode](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/unions/#union-modes), union members are validated differently but in all cases there is no constraint that it should only validate against only one member. A new union member could be introduced to do so (and then it would make sense to generate a `oneOf` schema for it), but this wasn't requested so far because the use case is pretty niche. --- I'll also note that FastAPI currently does _not_ support `type` arrays. The fix might be as simple as changing the [`Schema.type` definition](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/6df50d40fe195adc026af169d6ebf298a1c183a5/fastapi/openapi/models.py#L160) from `str | None` to `str | list[str] | None`, but there might be other things to consider. Reported in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/12787. [^1]: `{"type": ["array", "string"], "items": {"type": "string"}}` [^2]: `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}]}` [^3]: `{"type": ["object", "string"], "properties": {"f": {"type": "string"}}}` [^4]: `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "object", "properties": {"f": {"type": "string"}}}]}`

title: `HelpFormatter.write_usage` breaks options at a hyphen
issue_body:
If an option containing a hyphen in its name is printed at the line break limit, it’s broken at the hyphen.

### Reproduction

```python
import click

options = [
    "--enable-verbose-logging",
    "--output-file-path",
    "--max-retry-count",
    "--disable-cache-mode",
    "--config-file-location",
    "--user-auth-token",
    "--auto-update-interval",
    "--force-overwrite-existing",
    "--network-timeout-seconds",
    "--debug-trace-enabled",
]

f = click.HelpFormatter(width=65)
f.write_usage("program", " ".join(options))
print(f.getvalue())
```

### Expected output
```
Usage: program --enable-verbose-logging --output-file-path
               --max-retry-count --disable-cache-mode
               --config-file-location --user-auth-token
               --auto-update-interval --force-overwrite-existing
               --network-timeout-seconds --debug-trace-enabled
```

### Actual output
```
Usage: program --enable-verbose-logging --output-file-path --max-
               retry-count --disable-cache-mode --config-file-
               location --user-auth-token --auto-update-interval
               --force-overwrite-existing --network-timeout-
               seconds --debug-trace-enabled
```

### Environment

- Python version: 3.12.3
- Click version: 8.3.1

### Additional information

#### `width` option

This also happens without specifying `width`. The `width` option is altered in the example to make the issue more frequent.

#### Relevance to other use cases

This may likely only affect:

- direct users of `click.HelpFormatter`,
- users of `click.argument` with custom `metavar` containing hyphens. 

On the other hand, `click` prints `[OPTIONS]` instead of listing individual options on the usage line and uses underscores instead of hyphens in argument names (unless specifying `metavar`).

#### Cause

I looked into the code and found that `textwrap.TextWrapper` is used under the hood, which has the [`break_on_hyphens`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/textwrap.html#textwrap.TextWrapper.break_on_hyphens) option. However, there is no option for the `click` user to influence this, apart from reimplementing `HelpFormatter.write_usage` (in a subclass) and `wrap_text`.

---
PR Context (#3902):
Also fixes `write_usage` breaking a line inside an argument. Closes #3362.

Also reverts part of https://github.com/pallets/click/pull/3420 now that long words truncation is simplified.

title: Flask Session variable not available in threads

Session is a global variable

* Python version: 3.7
* Flask version: Default install
* Werkzeug version: Default install

title: `Response.location` and `content_location` should use `iri_to_uri`
issue_body:
They currently store strings, then call `iri_to_uri` in `get_wsgi_headers`. And that's only done for WSGI, so sans-IO/ASGI doesn't get it. Instead, they should always be stored as URIs, and accessed as IRIs.

No other headers are "fixed" in `get_wsgi_headers`. `Response.headers` is considered "raw" values, where it's the responsibility of the code setting it to set a valid value. That's what the properties provide: set a Python value, get the right encoded header value.

---
PR Context (#3327):
closes #3318 

`Response.location` and `content_location` properties use `iri_to_uri`. Deprecate doing so in `get_wsgi_headers`.

title: `useSyncExternalStore` doesn't resubscribe when `subscribe` function changes
issue_body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.12.31

### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible)

chrome 150.0.7871.181

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Clone repo https://github.com/pajecawav/hono-usesyncexternalstore-subscribe-repro
2. `pnpm install && pnpm dev` and open http://localhost:4173/
3. Click "Increment" 
4. Click "Reset"
5. New store is created but Hono is subscribed to the previous one so nothing happens

`useSyncExternalStore` accepts a `subscribe` function as a first argument to subscribe to the store change events, but doesn't resubscribe when the function changes. I believe the problem is that it uses `useEffect` without dependencies to subscribe to the store https://github.com/honojs/hono/blob/26d8e42bfff7eb78fc323a01e1d02d63b9dbcc72/src/jsx/hooks/index.ts#L415-L422

Hono demo:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be7fa615-136b-4c77-8632-2de3007b27de

### What is the expected behavior?

`useSyncExternalStore` resubscribes to the store when `subscribe` changes like react does

React demo from the same repo:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/955f8a6c-63bd-45b1-be4c-5114ad12de86

### What do you see instead?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

---
PR Context (#5166):
fixes #5162

The reported issue can be addressed by making the subscription effect depend on `subscribe`. This PR goes slightly further and also handles changes to `getSnapshot`:

- Re-subscribe when `subscribe` changes.
- Keep the previous subscription active until the new subscription is installed during the effect flush.
- Read the snapshot during render so a changed `getSnapshot` is reflected without waiting for a store notification.
- Re-check the latest snapshot after subscribing to avoid missing an update between render and effect execution.
- Add regression tests for changing `subscribe` and `getSnapshot`.

While investigating this, I also explored fixing the underlying deferred effect and cleanup behavior. Since that would affect all effect hooks and needs broader review, it is intentionally kept out of this PR; see the draft PoC in #5165.

title: PoolManager replaces the cached PoolKey on every request
issue_body:
### Subject

Each request through an existing pool replaces the cached `PoolKey` in `PoolManager.pools` with the new key of that request. `RecentlyUsedContainer.__getitem__()` uses `pop()` and a new insert under the key of the caller ([_collections.py#L93-L98](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/2.8.0/src/urllib3/_collections.py#L93-L98)).

Why this is a problem: the cached key must live as long as the pool. Instead, each request puts a new GC-tracked tuple in the cache. The young GC generation then scans the key again after each request, and a program that calls `gc.freeze()` cannot keep the key frozen.

### Environment

```
OS macOS-26.7.1-arm64-arm-64bit
Python 3.12.12
OpenSSL 3.5.4 30 Sep 2025
urllib3 2.8.0
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```python
import urllib3

pm = urllib3.PoolManager()
pm.connection_from_url("http://example.com/")  # no connection is opened
first_key = next(iter(pm.pools._container))

pm.connection_from_url("http://example.com/")
print(next(iter(pm.pools._container)) is first_key)
```

### Expected Behavior

`True`. The lookup keeps the cached key.

### Actual Behavior

`False`. The lookup replaced the cached key.

### Possible fix

`move_to_end()` keeps the eviction order and the cached key:

```diff
         with self.lock:
-            item = self._container.pop(key)
-            self._container[key] = item
+            item = self._container[key]
+            self._container.move_to_end(key)
             return item
```

I can open a PR with a test.

PR Context (#5347):

Thanks for your contribution! ♥️

If this is your first PR to urllib3 please review the Contributing Guide:
https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contributing.html

Adhering to the Contributing Guide means we can review, merge, and release your change faster! :)

Fixes #5346.

**TLDR:** A pool lookup no longer replaces the cached `PoolKey`. The key stays one long-lived object for the life of the pool.

### Why it matters

`PoolManager` builds a new `PoolKey` for each request, and the lookup stores this new key in the cache. As a result, each request to a known host leaves a new GC-tracked tuple that young-generation collections must scan. Programs that call `gc.freeze()` after warm-up lose the freeze on each pool key after the next request.

### Change

`RecentlyUsedContainer.__getitem__()` uses `move_to_end()` instead of `pop()` and a new insert. The eviction order does not change.

### Evidence

`check_key.py` makes one request, freezes the GC, and makes a second request to the same host. It does not open a connection.

```python
import gc
import urllib3

http = urllib3.PoolManager()
http.connection_from_url("https://example.com/")  # no connection is opened
gc.collect()
gc.freeze()
frozen_key = next(iter(http.pools._container))

http.connection_from_url("https://example.com/")
key = next(iter(http.pools._container))
print("cached key is the frozen key:", key is frozen_key)
print("cached key in GC generation 0:", any(o is key for o in gc.get_objects(generation=0)))
```

```bash
uv run --no-project --with urllib3==2.8.0 check_key.py
uv run --no-project --with "urllib3 @ git+https://github.com/zek/urllib3@fix-pool-key-replaced-on-lookup" check_key.py
```

| | Before fix (2.8.0) | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| `cached key is the frozen key` | `False` | **`True`** |
| `cached key in GC generation 0` | `True` | **`False`** |

title: fix(v4): let z.intersection merge cyclic outputs instead of overflowing
issue_body:
`z.intersection(A, B).safeParse(x)` threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` when `x` is cyclic and `A` and `B` are different recursive schemas. Each side parses the cycle into its own output graph, and merging them recursed around the cycle forever. The same schema on both sides was safe only because both sides hand back the same objects.

The merge now keeps the left/right pairs it has open, and a pair reached again closes the cycle with the merged object already in progress, so the result is cyclic like the input. Tracking starts only once a shared key holds objects on both sides, so a flat intersection allocates nothing new.

Cost: flat intersections are unchanged, a nested intersection with two shared object keys measured about 4% slower, and a `zod/mini` bundle that uses `z.intersection` grows by 64 B gzipped.

title: [BUG] `TableDataElement.on_text` clobbers syntax-highlight spans for inline code
issue_body:
- [x] I've checked [docs](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html) and [closed issues](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the [FAQ](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/FAQ.md).

When using `Markdown` with `inline_code_lexer` and `inline_code_theme`, inline code (backticks) inside table cells loses its syntax highlighting and falls back to the default `markdown.code` style. The same inline code renders correctly in paragraphs, headings, and list items.

**Root cause:**

`TableDataElement.on_text` (markdown.py) unconditionally applies `context.current_style` over the text:

```python
def on_text(self, context: MarkdownContext, text: TextType) -> None:
    text = Text(text) if isinstance(text, str) else text
    text.stylize(context.current_style)
    self.content.append_text(text)
```

When `MarkdownContext.on_text` processes a `code_inline` token, it produces a `Text` object with per-character syntax-highlight spans. But `TableDataElement.on_text` then calls `text.stylize(context.current_style)` on that `Text` object, which overwrites all the highlight spans with the flat `markdown.code` style.

Compare with `TextElement.on_text`, which correctly avoids this:

```python
def on_text(self, context: MarkdownContext, text: TextType) -> None:
    self.text.append(text, context.current_style if isinstance(text, str) else None)
```

Here, the style is only applied when `text` is a plain string. When it's already a highlighted `Text` object, `None` is passed, preserving the spans.

**Fix:**

`TableDataElement.on_text` should follow the same pattern:

```python
def on_text(self, context: MarkdownContext, text: TextType) -> None:
    if isinstance(text, str):
        self.content.append(text, context.current_style)
    else:
        self.content.append_text(text)
```

**Repro:**

```python
from rich.console import Console
from rich.markdown import Markdown

md = Markdown(
    "| Col |\n|---|\n| `hello` |\n\n`hello`",
    inline_code_theme="monokai",
    inline_code_lexer="python",
)
Console().print(md)
```

The standalone `` `hello` `` renders with the monokai theme; the one inside the table does not.

title: Quadratic behavior in `--report-chars=P`
issue_body:
When using `--report-chars=P`, the runtime of pytest seems to be growing quadratically with the number of tests.

From what I can see, this is a result of

* https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/50234b4e670064c42a4c29cb6258115a2079ba4c/src/_pytest/terminal.py#L1175 is triggered by `--report-chars=P`
* In the called function, we loop over all matching (passed, in this case) tests: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/50234b4e670064c42a4c29cb6258115a2079ba4c/src/_pytest/terminal.py#L1189
* For each test-report, we "handle" the teardown sections (see https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/50234b4e670064c42a4c29cb6258115a2079ba4c/src/_pytest/terminal.py#L1194)
* For this, we get all teardown reports based on the nodeId of the test; see https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/50234b4e670064c42a4c29cb6258115a2079ba4c/src/_pytest/terminal.py#L1205
* And to get all teardown reports based on the node-id, we iterate over *all* teardown reports: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/50234b4e670064c42a4c29cb6258115a2079ba4c/src/_pytest/terminal.py#L1198

Unrolling it all; it seems a lot like this shape:

```
for rep in reports:
    ....
    teardown_reports = [
       report for report in self.getreports("")
       if report.when == "teardown" and report.id = rep.id
    ]
    ...
```

The behavior is `O(number-of-passed-tests * number-of-all-reports)`, and also triggers for `xpassed`; though I assume `xpassed` is bounded in size and `passed` grows naturally when more tests are added.

In our case, dropping the `P` from `--report-chars` saved ~8 minutes.

Also fixes the rendering of help screen:
| Parameter value | Help screen before | Help screen after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `envvar=None` | Nothing | Nothing |

title: deprecate mixed string/bytes response iterable
issue_body:
`Response.response` has been annotated as `Iterable[bytes] | Iterable[str]` for a long time now. However, for historic reasons (Python 2's mixed str/bytes type, presumably), it can actually be a mixed `Iterable[bytes | str]`, because `Response.iter_encoded` does an instance check for every yielded item. While passing an iterable of strings is useful (for example, a generator with `csv.writer`), there should be absolutely no reason to have strings and bytes in the iterator. We could make `Response.iter_encoded` _hugely_ more efficient by only checking the type of the first item, then assuming it for the rest.

`direct_passthrough` is currently documented as useful for files, or for if you know the response is all bytes. With this change, it should only really be necessary for files/`wsgi.file_wrapper`. An iterator that just yields from another iterator (in the case of bytes) should be essentially no overhead.

---
PR Context (#3325):
- Mixed str/bytes iterable is deprecated. closes #3323 
- `Response.stream` is deprecated. closes #3324 
- `is_sequence` checks `Sequence` instead of only `list` or `tuple`. `is_streamed` checks `Sequence` instead of `len`.
- `make_sequence` closes the original iterable immediately rather than deferring it to close with the response.
- Use `calculate_content_length` consistently.
- `automatically_set_content_length` is deprecated.
- Rewrite all the docstrings that deal with the response iterable in some way.

title: Fix gzip multi-member decoding after a bounded read
issue_body:
`GzipDecoder.decompress()` stops once `max_length` bytes have been produced. If that point is exactly the end of a gzip member, the loop breaks before it swaps in a new decompressor. The next call then hands the remaining input to the finished one, zlib appends it to `unused_data` a second time, and the following member is returned over and over. For example, with two 100-byte members, `while resp.read(100): ...` never reaches EOF, and `read1(1)` on `gzip.compress(b"A") + gzip.compress(b"B")` loops the same way.

The end-of-member check now runs before the `max_length` break, so the decoder is ready when the next call arrives. The `max_length` break was added with the decompression-bomb safeguards in c19571d.

Added `test_decode_gzip_multi_member_with_max_length`: it reads two 1 KiB members with `read(1024)`, and with `read1(1024)`, and fails on main at the last call, which returns more `y` bytes instead of `b""`. `test/test_response.py` passes, and black, isort and flake8 are clean.

@@ -0,0 +1,352 @@
+import asyncio
+from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
+from threading import Event, get_ident
+from traceback import extract_tb
+from types import TracebackType
+from typing import Literal
+
+import anyio
+import anyio.from_thread
+import anyio.to_thread
+import httpx
+import pytest
+from anyio import wait_all_tasks_blocked
+from anyio.abc import TaskStatus
+from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
+from fastapi.concurrency import contextmanager_in_threadpool
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.anyio
+
+
+class BaseError(BaseException):
+    pass
+
+
+class RecordingContextManager(AbstractContextManager[str]):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        enter_error: BaseException | None = None,
+        exit_error: BaseException | None = None,
+        suppress: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.enter_error = enter_error
+        self.exit_error = exit_error
+        self.suppress = suppress
+        self.enter_threads: list[int] = []
+        self.exit_threads: list[int] = []
+        self.exit_args: list[
+            tuple[
+                type[BaseException] | None, BaseException | None, TracebackType | None
+            ]
+        ] = []
+
+    def __enter__(self) -> str:
+        self.enter_threads.append(get_ident())
+        if self.enter_error is not None:
+            raise self.enter_error
+        return "value"
+
+    def __exit__(
+        self,
+        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
+        exc_value: BaseException | None,
+        traceback: TracebackType | None,
+    ) -> bool:
+        self.exit_threads.append(get_ident())
+        self.exit_args.append((exc_type, exc_value, traceback))
+        if self.exit_error is not None:
+            raise self.exit_error
+        return self.suppress
+
+
+def assert_exited_in_worker(cm: RecordingContextManager) -> None:
+    assert len(cm.exit_threads) == 1
+    assert cm.exit_threads[0] != get_ident()
+
+
+async def test_contextmanager_returns_value_and_exits_in_worker() -> None:
+    cm = RecordingContextManager()
+    async with contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm) as value:
+        assert value == "value"
+    assert cm.enter_threads[0] != get_ident()
+    assert_exited_in_worker(cm)
+    assert cm.exit_args == [(None, None, None)]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("error_type", [ValueError, BaseError])
+async def test_failed_enter_does_not_call_exit(
+    error_type: type[BaseException],
+) -> None:
+    error = error_type("entry failed")
+    cm = RecordingContextManager(enter_error=error)
+    with pytest.raises(error_type) as caught:
+        async with contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm):
+            pytest.fail("Entry should fail")  # pragma: no cover
+    assert caught.value is error
+    assert cm.exit_threads == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("error_type", [ValueError, BaseError])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("suppress", [False, True])
+async def test_exit_receives_body_exception(
+    error_type: type[BaseException], suppress: bool
+) -> None:
+    error = error_type("body failed")
+    cm = RecordingContextManager(suppress=suppress)
+
+    async def use() -> None:
+        async with contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm):
+            raise error
+
+    if suppress:
+        await use()
+    else:
+        with pytest.raises(error_type) as caught:
+            await use()
+        assert caught.value is error
+    assert_exited_in_worker(cm)
+    exc_type, exc_value, traceback = cm.exit_args[0]
+    assert exc_type is error_type
+    assert exc_value is error
+    assert traceback is not None
+    assert extract_tb(traceback)[-1].name == "use"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("body_state", ["success", "exception", "cancelled"])
+async def test_cleanup_exception_propagates(body_state: str) -> None:
+    error = ValueError("cleanup failed")
+    cm = RecordingContextManager(exit_error=error)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as caught, anyio.CancelScope() as scope:
+        async with contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm):
+            if body_state == "exception":
+                raise RuntimeError("body failed")
+            if body_state == "cancelled":
+                scope.cancel()
+                await anyio.sleep(0)
+    assert caught.value is error
+    assert_exited_in_worker(cm)
+    if body_state == "exception":
+        assert isinstance(error.__context__, RuntimeError)
+    elif body_state == "cancelled":
+        assert isinstance(error.__context__, anyio.get_cancelled_exc_class())
+
+
+async def test_cancelled_body_exits_in_worker() -> None:
+    cm = RecordingContextManager()
+    with anyio.CancelScope() as scope:
+        async with contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm):
+            scope.cancel()

+    assert_exited_in_worker(cm)
+    assert isinstance(cm.exit_args[0][1], anyio.get_cancelled_exc_class())

+async def test_cancelled_scope_exits_before_next_checkpoint() -> None:
+    cm = RecordingContextManager()

+    assert_exited_in_worker(cm)
+    assert cm.exit_args == [(None, None, None)]

+async def test_cancelled_wait_for_worker_does_not_enter_or_exit() -> None:
+    cm = RecordingContextManager()
+    limiter = anyio.to_thread.current_default_thread_limiter()
+    original_tokens = limiter.total_tokens
+    limiter.total_tokens = 1
+    finished = anyio.Event()

+            task_status.started(scope)

+    assert cm.exit_threads == []

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cancel_during", ["enter", "exit"])
+async def test_cancellation_waits_for_worker_and_cleanup(cancel_during: str) -> None:
+    started = anyio.Event()
+    release = Event()
+    finished = anyio.Event()
+
+    def wait_in_worker() -> None:
+        anyio.from_thread.run_sync(started.set)
+        assert release.wait(5)
+
+    class BlockingContextManager(RecordingContextManager):
+        def __enter__(self) -> str:
+            if cancel_during == "enter":
+                wait_in_worker()
+            return super().__enter__()
+
+        def __exit__(
+            self,
+            exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
+            exc_value: BaseException | None,
+            traceback: TracebackType | None,
+        ) -> bool:
+            if cancel_during == "exit":
+                wait_in_worker()
+            return super().__exit__(exc_type, exc_value, traceback)
+
+    cm = BlockingContextManager()
+
+    async def use(*, task_status: TaskStatus[anyio.CancelScope]) -> None:
+        with anyio.CancelScope() as scope:
+            task_status.started(scope)
+            async with contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm):
+                await anyio.sleep(0)
+        finished.set()
+
+    async with anyio.create_task_group() as group:
+        try:
+            scope = await group.start(use)
+            with anyio.fail_after(2):
+                await started.wait()
+            scope.cancel()
+            await wait_all_tasks_blocked()
+            assert not finished.is_set()
+        finally:
+            release.set()
+        with anyio.fail_after(2):
+            await finished.wait()
+    assert_exited_in_worker(cm)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cancel", [False, True])
+async def test_cleanup_does_not_need_default_worker_capacity(cancel: bool) -> None:
+    cm = RecordingContextManager()
+    limiter = anyio.to_thread.current_default_thread_limiter()
+    original_tokens = limiter.total_tokens
+    limiter.total_tokens = 1
+    entered = anyio.Event()
+    capacity_held = anyio.Event()
+    release_capacity = anyio.Event()
+    finished = anyio.Event()

+        await entered.wait()
+        async with limiter:
+            capacity_held.set()
+            await release_capacity.wait()
+
+    async def use() -> None:
+        with anyio.CancelScope() as scope:
+            async with contextmanager_in_threadpool(cm):
+                entered.set()
+                await capacity_held.wait()
+                if cancel:
+                    scope.cancel()
+                    await anyio.sleep(0)
+        finished.set()
+
+    try:
+        async with anyio.create_task_group() as group:

+                group.start_soon(hold_capacity)

+    finally:
+        task.cancel()
+    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+        await task
+    assert_exited_in_worker(cm)
+    assert isinstance(cm.exit_args[0][1], asyncio.CancelledError)

title: fix(v4): stop shared nodes from doubling the issue count per level
issue_body:
When a failing node is reachable by more than one path, the memoizer replays its issues at every repeat visit. Through n levels of shared references that doubles at each level, so one bad leaf under 18 levels of diamonds produced 262,144 issues, and around 20 to 40 levels the parse runs out of memory.

A visit that recorded more than 100 issues now keeps one for its repeat visits, the first aborting issue if there is one so a parent still skips its own checks. Shared nodes with 100 issues or fewer still report at every path, as before. The 18-level case now produces 139 issues, and the count grows by one per level past the limit.

Valid input never reaches the changed code. `zod/mini` with the memoizer grows by 50 B gzipped, and failing parses of recursive schemas measured within noise.
